Traupman 86

semper

adverb

For a habit, Latin often prefers soleō: ut soleō, as I always do (Cic. Att. 2.8.1).

Other words

  • numquam nōn — always (never not)

    also used · classical · Quint. 1.1.20: numquam nōn fēcisse sē gaudeat

Examples

  • crās tē vīctūrum, crās dīcis, Postume, semper: dīc mihi, crās istud, Postume, quandō venit?

    ‘Tomorrow I’ll start living,’ you always say, Postumus, ‘tomorrow’: tell me, Postumus, when does this tomorrow come?Mart. 5.58.1–2

  • Cicerō meus quid aget? iste vērō sit in sinū semper et complexū meō

    and what will my little Cicero do? Let him always be in my lap and in my armsCic. Fam. 14.4.3

See also never, every year, every night, as usual.

SourcesLewis & Short: semper · Lewis & Short: soleo
